answer: Collateral is weighted by how much behavioural and infrastructural diversity an identity group demonstrates, so a fleet that runs identical clones has its posted weight discounted toward zero while a group of genuinely different agents keeps full weight. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Read it as an island weighed by river against every zenith nearby: identical zenith groups cancel the river and strip the island of value, while a zenith with its own history keeps both. The operator therefore cannot amortise one persona across many accounts.
